title: Integrated Antioxidants, Nanoparticle, and Antifreeze Protein Strategies Synergistically Enhance Cryotop Vitrification Outcomes of Porcine Parthenogenetic Embryos.
study_design: Sequential Cryotop vitrification optimization with culture-stage antioxidants, vitrification-stage ice/particle additives, and post-warming recovery refinements; experiments repeated at least three times.
interventions: berberine 2.5 μM and melatonin 10−9 M during culture
Fe3O4 nanoparticles 1.0% and AFP I 500 ng/mL during equilibration/vitrification
post-warm glutathione 5 mM and trypsin zona treatment 45 s

experiments.intervention: Berberine, melatonin, Fe3O4 and AFP I were compared individually and in paired combinations across culture and vitrification stages.
experiments.comparator: Cryotop-only frozen control and fresh control
experiments.cooling: TL-PVA with 7.5% DMSO/7.5% EG for 3 min at reported 41 °C, then 16% DMSO/16% EG/0.4 M sucrose for 30 s; Cryotop plunge; measured rate not reported
experiments.warming: Reported 39 °C thawing solution; morphology survival at 24 h culture, hatching at blastocyst stage
experiments.outcome_name: Post-thaw survival, hatching, cytoskeletal integrity, ROS and ATP
experiments.timepoint: Morphological survival 24 h post-warm; hatching at blastocyst stage
experiments.result: Fe3O4+AFP I and berberine+melatonin each improved survival and quality endpoints versus Cryotop-only controls; the paired arms exceeded either component alone where directly compared. Each additive improved measured endpoints versus Cryotop-only; paired Fe3O4+AFP I had survival 84.44% (228/270) versus 72.97% (197/270) Cryotop-only, while berberine+melatonin had survival 87.80% (252/287) versus 70.00% (245/350).
experiments.sample_size: Table 4–5 report embryo numerators/denominators; experiments repeated at least three times.
experiments.evidence_excerpt: combined Fe 3 O 4 + AFP I group

experiments.model: Frozen–thawed porcine parthenotes after integrated protocol and post-warm refinements
experiments.intervention: Sequential experiments: integrated culture/freezing additives (Table 6), then 5 mM GSH and 45-second zona treatment (Table 9); do not merge as one factorial experiment
experiments.comparator: Cryotop frozen control and fresh no-freeze control
experiments.cooling: TL-PVA with 7.5% DMSO/7.5% EG for 3 min at reported 41 °C, then 16% DMSO/16% EG/0.4 M sucrose for 30 s; Cryotop plunge; measured rate not reported
experiments.warming: Reported 39 °C thawing solution; morphology survival at 24 h culture, hatching at blastocyst stage
experiments.timepoint: post-warming culture through hatching; ATP/ROS and gene expression endpoints as tabulated
experiments.result: Table 6 reports integrated-group survival 93.75% and hatching 90.48%; Table 9 separately reports 90.70% hatching with GSH plus 45-second zona treatment. These are distinct experiments with endpoint-specific denominators. Nonsignificant differences versus fresh controls are not equivalence evidence.
experiments.sample_size: Table 6 and Table 9 provide endpoint-specific embryo denominators; molecular assays n=30.

main_finding: Combining culture-stage antioxidants with vitrification additives and post-warm recovery treatment improved porcine parthenote survival, hatching and injury-associated quality markers.
limitations: Parthenogenetic porcine embryos are an animal model; endpoint denominators differ across assays and the study does not establish transfer or offspring outcomes.
Survival is a morphological embryo fraction at 24 h, not absolute live-cell yield; hatching is affected directly by zona digestion and does not establish implantation/live birth.
No direct ice-growth/ice-content assay or external magnetic heating intervention is established here; physical mechanisms for AFP/nanoparticles are interpretations, not demonstrated nanowarming.
Methods use one-way ANOVA/Tukey comparisons, not a factorial interaction or equivalence test. Highest combination mean does not establish supra-additive synergy.
Reported group mean percentages and parenthetical aggregate counts do not always reconcile; replicate-level data are needed to distinguish aggregation from reporting errors.
Table 6 fresh-control cytoskeleton/ROS cells appear misaligned; values are preserved without repair and excluded from mechanistic comparisons.
Source describes Fe3O4 as 1.0% without a clear concentration basis in the extracted methods; particle size/coating/lot and independent maternal/replicate identities require confirmation.
mechanism_claim: Reduced ROS, altered transcripts, ATP and morphology support injury-associated benefit; direct ice mechanisms and target engagement are not established. Combination gains are reported group comparisons, not a validated synergy model.
reviewer: Luna extraction; root selected methods/results and interpretation review

title: Cryopreservation and post-thaw differentiation of monocytes enabled by macromolecular cryoprotectants which restrict intracellular ice formation.
cell_types: THP-1 human monocytic leukemia cell line
study_design: Cryovial and 96-well plate cryopreservation were compared with DMSO and commercial CS5, followed by post-thaw growth, apoptosis, Cryo-Raman intracellular ice imaging, and macrophage differentiation.
interventions: 96-well formulation additionally containing 50% pollen-derived ice nucleator solution

experiments.intervention: Polyampholyte added to 5% DMSO/20% FBS cryomedium.
experiments.warming: Thawed into fresh pre-warmed medium; recovery measured immediately and at 24 h.
experiments.timepoint: immediately post-thaw and 24 h post-thaw; growth monitored to 96 h
experiments.result: Polyampholyte supplementation preserved 24-h recovery and growth relative to DMSO-only and CS5 cryovial controls. At 24 h, intact-membrane recovery was 77% with DMSO+polyampholyte versus 34% with DMSO and 17% with CS5; polyampholyte growth approximated fresh cells over 96 h.
experiments.sample_size: 3 biological repeats and 2 technical replicates; starting density 1×10^6 viable cells/mL.

experiments.model: THP-1 cells cryopreserved in u-bottom 96-well plates
experiments.intervention: 5% DMSO + 40 mg/mL polyampholyte + 50% pollen ice-nucleator solution.
experiments.cooling: −80 °C for at least 24 h in CoolSink XT module.
experiments.warming: Plate thaw: add warm medium, incubate at 37 °C for 12 min, remove CPA and culture; Raman is a separate controlled-cooling assay
experiments.outcome_name: Well-level recovery, apoptosis and intracellular ice
experiments.timepoint: 24 h post-thaw recovery; intracellular ice measured during controlled cooling
experiments.result: Polyampholyte plus pollen ice nucleator increased plate recovery and reduced intracellular ice relative to DMSO-only and CS5 controls. Median 24-h recovery was 76% with polyampholyte+ice nucleator versus 37% DMSO and 30% CS5; Cryo-Raman showed markedly less intracellular ice with polyampholyte. Subsequent PMA-induced macrophage-like morphology and marker expression were assessed; these do not by themselves establish immune effector potency. Raman percentages are image-based relative ice estimates in five cells per condition, not a population incidence of ice-positive cells.
experiments.sample_size: 3 biological and 2 technical replicates for plate assays; Raman showed 5 individual cells per condition.
experiments.evidence_excerpt: estimation of relative ice formation per cell
experiments.source_locator: PMC12147442, Results ‘chemical ice nucleator’ and Fig. 2–3

main_finding: Macromolecular polyampholyte and pollen-derived ice nucleator additives improved delayed THP-1 recovery and limited intracellular ice in cryovial and plate formats.
limitations: THP-1 is an immortalized monocytic leukemia line rather than primary monocytes; recovery, apoptosis and Raman assays have distinct denominators.

Polyampholyte chemistry is a modified poly(methyl vinyl ether-alt-maleic anhydride) starting from approximately 80 kDa material; exact composition/charge balance/lot specification matters, not any polymer labeled polyampholyte.
This is THP-1 monocytic leukemia-line evidence; three biological repeats are not three human donors.
Cryovials compare polyampholyte addition; plate experiments also add pollen-derived ice nucleator, so the plate gain cannot be attributed solely to polymer chemistry.
Cryo-Raman uses five individual cells per condition; text wording about percentages of cells should not be read as a population incidence estimate.
Post-thaw differentiation markers are supportive phenotype endpoints; no matched primary-monocyte/iPSC efficacy or comprehensive macrophage potency validation is established.
Storage demonstrated here is about 24 h at −80 °C; longer banking durability remains unverified in these experiments.
mechanism_claim: Cryo-Raman directly measured intracellular ice signatures; reduced apoptosis and improved recovery are biological outcomes associated with the formulation, not proof of a unique pathway.
reviewer: Luna extraction; root selected methods/results and interpretation review
